paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.

model_annotations.English: The chart illustrates negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens, showing grouped bars for token sets associated with different clinical specialties and multiple model variants (a baseline model and versions fine-tuned on specialty-specific data). The category axis is horizontal and labeled “Per-specialty terms,” with six groups ordered left to right as Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The value axis is vertical and labeled “Negative log probability,” displayed on a linear scale with tick labels from approximately −27 up to −22 at roughly 1-unit intervals. Each specialty group contains seven adjacent vertical bars corresponding to the legend: a light-blue “Mistralv0.2-Base” bar plus six fine-tuned variants colored from very light peach through progressively darker oranges to dark brown (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics). In the Cardio group, the baseline bar extends to about −26.8, while the fine-tuned bars cluster near roughly −25.7 to −26.1 (darkest brown around −26.1). In the Gastro group, the baseline is around −24.8 and the fine-tuned bars fall around approximately −23.9 to −24.3 (with the darkest brown near ~−24.2). In the Infect group, the baseline is near −23.7 and the fine-tuned bars are around ~−23.0 to ~−23.3 (darkest brown near ~−23.3). In the Neuro group, the baseline is about −25.4 and the fine-tuned bars range around ~−24.1 to ~−24.7 (darkest brown near ~−24.7). In the Obstetrics group, the baseline is around −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars are about ~−23.8 to ~−24.1 (darkest brown near ~−24.1). In the Pediatrics group, the baseline is around −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars appear around ~−23.6 to ~−24.0 (darkest brown near ~−24.0). The bars are grouped by specialty rather than being sorted by height, and there are no visible outlines, callouts, or special emphasis beyond the color legend.

The vertical axis is labeled “Negative log probability,” uses a linear numeric scale, and spans approximately from −27 at the bottom to −22 at the top with tick labels shown at integer intervals (−22, −23, −24, −25, −26, −27). In the Cardio token group, the baseline bar is near −26.8, while the fine-tuned variants cluster around roughly −25.7 to −26.1 (with the darkest brown Pediatrics fine-tune near about −26.1). In the Gastro group, the baseline is around −24.8 and the fine-tuned bars lie near approximately −23.8 to −24.2 (with the darkest brown near about −24.2). In the Infect group, the baseline is around −23.7 and the fine-tuned bars sit around roughly −22.9 to −23.2 (darkest brown near about −23.2). In the Neuro group, the baseline is near −25.4 and the fine-tuned bars are around approximately −24.2 to −24.7 (darkest brown near about −24.7). In the Obstetrics group, the baseline is around −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars are near roughly −23.8 to −24.1 (darkest brown near about −24.1). In the Pediatrics group, the baseline is around −24.7 and the fine-tuned bars are approximately −23.6 to −24.0 (darkest brown near about −24.0). The bars are arranged by specialty group rather than being sorted by bar height, and there are no visible callouts, outlines, or special emphasis beyond the color-coding and the grouped layout.
